# E1 Phase R7: sensitivity analyses requested by reviewers

**SENSITIVITY.** No hypothesis, no decision rule, no verdict. Definitions: `docs/records/decisions.md`, "Phase R7 (sensitivity, specified before the runs)". Generated by `src/make_r7_summary.py`. Money is USD/yr. Value = mean over the 50 test seeds of net minus no cleaning. Every policy is retuned on the training years in every variant. Counts are "mean above 0 / interval wholly above 0 / interval wholly below 0" over the 56 case-years, with paired 95% t-intervals over the 50 seeds. Qualifying case-years: the 30 with R6 oracle value at or above 1,000 USD/yr.

Stored baseline (R3 to R5, F2, defaults): planner minus FT 25 / 20 / 25; FT minus plain 31 / 27 / 18.

## 4. Which information makes up the headroom (r7_oracle_split)

The 30 qualifying case-years, seeds 0 to 9 only (the first 10, to bound runtime). Every oracle is an open-loop full-year plan, scored in the simulator. C: the stored R6 oracle (perfect prices, rain, dust and per-row soiling). A: perfect prices, rain only through the policies' rain forecast flags (closest valid variant; it sees all flags of the year but never the realised rain). B: F2 prices, perfect rain. D: perfect prices and rain, per-row soiling replaced by the station estimate. The R6 oracle uses per-row true soiling. Share = mean policy value / mean oracle value over these seeds.

What this split can and cannot separate. C is an upper bound on every policy (a full-information optimum). A, B and D are not: each is a fixed full-year plan made with one kind of information removed, while the policies see that information as the year unfolds (they observe rain after it falls, prices up to the day, and the measured soiling). A share above 100% against A, B or D means the policy beat that fixed plan. C minus A, C minus B and C minus D are therefore the value of each kind of information to a fixed full-year plan, not the part of the policies' gap to C caused by that kind of information. Each kind is removed alone, so the three losses need not add up to anything and are not a decomposition. The oracle cannot separate the value of reacting to observations from the value of the information itself.

## 6. Sanity checks

- The F2 arm reproduces the stored R3 to R5 per-seed nets of plain, FT and planner: differs in 0 of 56 case-years. No-cleaning nets differ between forecast arms in 0 case-years; the plain threshold's nets differ from F2 in 0 case-year-arms (it reads no prices).
- F4 FT worse than F2 FT by more than 500 USD/yr (case-year mean value): 0 of 56. Lowest: Roma ppa 2025, -112 USD/yr; FT tuned to {'Hb': 14, 'antic': 0, 'b': 4} under F4 and {'Hb': 14, 'antic': 0, 'b': 8} under F2, training-year mean net 55445 and 55451. Not triggered.
- Oracle C (stored R6, full information) below the best policy: 0 of 300 seeds, 0 case-years on means. Not triggered.
- Identical inputs, oracle C: largest difference between its no-cleaning net and the stored policies' no-cleaning net: 0.00e+00 USD.
- Oracle A below the best policy: 258 of 300 seeds, 30 case-years on means. Expected, not a bug: A plans with less information than the policies in one respect (realised rain) and is an open-loop plan, while the policies react to observations.
- Oracle A above oracle C: 0 of 300 seeds (largest difference A minus C: -67.04 USD); above C's Lagrangian upper bound: 0. Not triggered.
- Identical inputs, oracle A: largest difference between its no-cleaning net and the stored policies' no-cleaning net: 0.00e+00 USD.
- Oracle B below the best policy: 23 of 300 seeds, 0 case-years on means. Expected, not a bug: B plans with less information than the policies in one respect (prices beyond the F2 forecast) and is an open-loop plan, while the policies react to observations.
- Oracle B above oracle C: 0 of 300 seeds (largest difference B minus C: -0.19 USD); above C's Lagrangian upper bound: 0. Not triggered.
- Identical inputs, oracle B: largest difference between its no-cleaning net and the stored policies' no-cleaning net: 0.00e+00 USD.
- Oracle D below the best policy: 0 of 300 seeds, 0 case-years on means. Not triggered.
- Oracle D above oracle C: 92 of 300 seeds (largest difference D minus C: +37.40 USD); above C's Lagrangian upper bound: 0. Not a bug: C is a local-search optimum within its bound (median gap to the bound 41.3 USD), and the D search sometimes ends on a better true schedule.
- Identical inputs, oracle D: largest difference between its no-cleaning net and the stored policies' no-cleaning net: 0.00e+00 USD.
